audit.verification: The real carousel façade and pier railing visibly match the episode frame. The conservation source confirms 276 Santa Monica Pier. Coordinate is the mapped Hippodrome landmark, not a survey of the actors’ precise positions. Seeing Stars describes a Venice Boardwalk stand-in, but no Venice claim occurs in the aired dialogue transcript. The transcript’s editorial scene headings say Santa Monica, while cast commentary at 27:52–28:11 explains importing Venice-style beach culture to the Santa Monica shoot. The record retains the visible pier and audits this disagreement rather than asserting an unsupported Venice address.

Seeing Stars identifies the exterior as Metro Headquarters and the office interior from its skyline view as Wells Fargo’s south tower. One story headquarters is retained, with two labelled productionSites. Janeway/Chakotay enter Starling’s office; the Doctor is held there, and the Aeon launches from the headquarters in Part II. The exterior pin uses the building area shown in the source-linked map; Census verifies the One Gateway Plaza address but interpolates to a nearby road point. No canonical street address is inferred. The later van shot labelled outside Chronowerx was filmed near the Music Center and is not used to create a second headquarters.

Seeing Stars matches the crew’s coastal walk to the park’s southern end by the cannon, with a second frame looking toward Ocean Avenue near Colorado. The SUVCW landmark inventory, printed page 125, independently locates the cannon at 34.01143, -118.49556. Coordinates mark the southern park area, not a citywide park centroid. The 2023 real photo shows the same park and coast, from another section; it is not presented as the exact camera position.

Part II’s spoken dialogue explicitly names Metro Plaza by the fountain. Visual comparisons identify the Music Center’s Grand Avenue steps and Hope Street plaza edge; the Doctor’s frame includes the fountain/sculpture/City Hall view. The production point comes from the source-linked matching plaza view. Census independently matches 135 N Grand Avenue but its road interpolation is not the scene viewpoint. No claim is made that the Music Center’s official real name is Metro Plaza. The owner’s plaza history confirms 2018–2019 renovation and relocation of Peace on Earth.

All four records use the episode’s explicit local Earth year 1996. The starship travellers’ 24th-century origin is not used to date these visits. Existing Rain Robinson / Griffith Observatory record 83 is not duplicated.

Four actual episode frames were downloaded directly from Gary Wayne’s scene guide and visually inspected against the real place. Ground photographs: pier from Santa Monica Pier Corporation via the Conservancy (capture date unknown); Metro HQ by Busition, 2026-05-08, CC BY 4.0; Palisades Park by Z3lvs, 2023-03-20, CC0; renovated Music Center plaza by Tim Street-Porter (capture date unknown). Only source borders and file encoding/size were adjusted; no generated photos.

Excluded: Lancaster/30th Street West footage explicitly representing Arizona; the 1967 High Sierras prologue; and the proposed Paramount lunch-lawn identification, which the location researcher describes as a suspicion rather than a verified match.
